C0.quote: members of an advisory committee with private continuous signals vote on a policy change
C0.note: Strategic voting game: committee votes, decision maker aggregates votes via decision rules (k-rules, weighted voting); equilibrium and information aggregation analysis.

C1.quote: necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of an informative equilibrium
C1.note: Main results are equilibrium existence characterisations (Props 2-3); Prop 4 on full information aggregation is a performance/welfare-like result (mistake probabilities vanish).

C2.1.quote: maps a vote profile v := (v1, … , vn) ∈ {Y, N}

C2.2.quote: votes simultaneously over the two options
C2.2.note: Binary votes Y/N on two policy options; none of the listed formats exactly (a binary vote).

C2.3.quote: Each member i (he) receives a private signal si about the state
C2.3.note: Held attitudes: private signals and payoffs/preferences over decisions given state.

C2.4.quote: A voting strategy of member i is a (measurable) function
C2.4.note: Signals/payoffs are separate from votes; vote is a strategy mapping signal to vote probability.

C3.1.quote: committee members must use a cutoff strategy
C3.1.note: All analyses model members as strategic Bayesian voters in equilibrium.

C4.1.note: Input is a binary vote, no RANK/WEAK/APPR/DICH/PAIR format.

C5.1.note: Full information aggregation, probability of DM making mistakes vanishes, evaluates rules by decision accuracy relative to the state, matching payoffs of committee and DM; borderline against the listed criteria.

C5.2.quote: probabilities of the DM choosing Y in state y and N in state n
C5.2.note: Evaluated against the true state, defined separately from votes.

VOT.quote_behav: must be indifferent between voting for Y and N conditional on being pivotal
VOT.quote_info: receives a private signal si about the state θ
VOT.note: Committee members observe private signals and common prior, not others' signals.

DES.note: The DM is a player, coded under OTH.

OTH.quote_behav: The DM (she) makes the final decision D ∈ {Y, N}
OTH.note: Other agent: decision maker who chooses a decision rule/decision in PBE (best responds to beliefs); observes votes but not signals; knows prior.

C7.1.note: Both voters and DM are strategic.

C8.1.quote: We use perfect Bayesian equilibrium (PBE) as the solution concept.
C8.1.note: Perfect Bayesian equilibrium of a sequential voting-then-decision game; coded as BNE/SPE-type; named PBE.

C8.2.quote: We use perfect Bayesian equilibrium (PBE) as the solution concept.

claims.quote: offers a new rationale, from the perspective of information transmission, why the unanimity rule
Corollary 1 thus rationalizes the pressure for a higher level of consensus

C9.1.note: Claims about institutions and which rule is prevalent.

C9.2.quote: unanimity rule is so prevailing in decision-making processes
C9.2.note: Claims about real institutions rely on assumptions such as the DM being unable to commit and rule being endogenous, which are stated; but the link from the model to real committees (e.g. homogeneous members, continuous signals) is only partly argued; some applicability assumptions unstated.
